label: Two Raspberry Pi Pico 2s
detail: The real-time controllers, socketed on the underside: one runs the motors, winch and RC, the other the sensors, GPS and the pod link. Only their header holes show here.

label: Raspberry Pi 5 socket
detail: The Pi plugs in here, face down on standoffs. The header carries its 5 V power, a serial link to the control Pico and a reset line for each Pico.

label: CAN link to motor controllers
detail: TJA1051 transceiver and a 3-pin connector to the two VESC motor controllers, plus a jumper for the 120 Ω terminator.

label: I²C sensor multiplexer
detail: TCA9548A splits one I²C bus into 8 channels: IMU, accelerometer, light sensor, two humidity sensors, power monitors, GPS compass.

label: Sensor-pod link (RS-485)
detail: THVD2410 transceiver and a 4-pin connector for the tether to the water-sensing pod. The same cable carries 15 V to power the pod.

label: GPS connector
detail: 6-pin cable socket for the u-blox M10 GPS module: serial data plus the I²C lines of its built-in compass.

label: RC receiver input (SBUS)
detail: 3-pin socket for the radio-control receiver, the manual override. Its 5 V supply is fused loosely so it never nuisance-trips.

label: Battery inputs
detail: Two XT60 connectors take the boat's 10S battery bus: one feed for the electronics, and one for the winch used in the later sample-collection stage. A 5 V buck regulator module on the left powers the Pi and both Picos.

label: Battery monitors (INA228)
detail: Two INA228 chips with shunt resistors measure voltage and current on the electronics pack and the winch pack.

label: Winch safety cut-off
detail: A P-channel MOSFET switches power to the winch controller and fails safe: if the Teensy resets or loses power, the winch is off. A red LED shows it is live.

label: Backup battery input
detail: An optional small 4S battery plugs in at the board's left edge. If the main packs go off, it keeps the Pi, both Picos and the radios running.
